report.incidentSummary: Starting around 2026-10-16 10:40 IST (05:10 UTC), users experienced OTP login failures. The OTP success rate dropped from ~97.5% down to ~68% and auth-service error rate rose to ~4.5%, while notification-service successfully accepted SMS requests.
report.rootCauseStatement: Upstream SMS provider delivery degradation or carrier-level filtering delays prevented users from receiving OTP SMS messages, causing login attempts to fail even though notification-service successfully received HTTP 202 responses from the provider.

hypotheses.cause: Upstream SMS provider delivery degradation or carrier-level filtering delays
hypotheses.rationale: OTP success rate dropped while notification-service successfully submitted SMS requests to the provider (HTTP 202). Historical incidents show identical symptoms due to external SMS provider issues.

hypotheses.cause: Elevated failed client OTP verification attempts due to delayed SMS delivery
hypotheses.rationale: auth-service error rate increased simultaneously, but logs showed no internal server errors (5xx), pointing toward client-side or verification failures resulting from missing codes.

facts.statement: auth-service otp_success_rate dropped from ~97.5% to ~68% starting around 2026-10-16T05:10:00.000Z.
auth-service error rate increased from ~0.5% to ~4.5% starting at 2026-10-16T05:10:00.000Z.
notification-service logs show SMS messages accepted by sms-provider with status 202 during the incident window.
No deployments or configuration updates occurred on auth-service or notification-service prior to the incident.
Historical incidents (PIR-2004, PIR-1602) indicate external SMS provider routing or delivery failures cause identical drops in OTP success rates.

inferences.statement: API acceptance (HTTP 202) by the SMS provider without successful downstream carrier delivery explains the drop in OTP success rates without a spike in notification-service error metrics.

assumptions.statement: The external SMS provider experienced downstream carrier delivery failures or severe DLR latency during the incident window.

confidence.rationale: Supported by metrics, logs showing successful API acceptance by the SMS provider, and strong historical precedent (PIR-2004, PIR-1602). Direct carrier delivery logs are missing, relying on indirect inference.

recommendedActions.rationale: API requests returned 202 Accepted, indicating the issue lies downstream of the provider API.
recommendedActions.verification: SMS provider confirms normal DLR rates and carrier delivery times.

recommendedActions.rationale: Historical incidents (PIR-2004) successfully resolved via secondary provider failover.

payload.markdown:
# Investigation report: OTP logins failing

**Outcome:** conclusive · **Stop reason:** critic_accepted · **Confidence:** 0.75 · **Written by:** reporting agent

## Summary
Starting around 2026-10-16 10:40 IST (05:10 UTC), users experienced OTP login failures. The OTP success rate dropped from ~97.5% down to ~68% and auth-service error rate rose to ~4.5%, while notification-service successfully accepted SMS requests.

**Root cause:** Upstream SMS provider delivery degradation or carrier-level filtering delays prevented users from receiving OTP SMS messages, causing login attempts to fail even though notification-service successfully received HTTP 202 responses from the provider.

## Hypotheses
1. **Upstream SMS provider delivery degradation or carrier-level filtering delays** — `sms-provider`, upstream_dependency_degradation, confidence 0.75, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_3, ev_6, ev_7, ev_8, ev_12, ev_15, ev_16] · Contradicting: none
   - OTP success rate dropped while notification-service successfully submitted SMS requests to the provider (HTTP 202). Historical incidents show identical symptoms due to external SMS provider issues.
2. **Elevated failed client OTP verification attempts due to delayed SMS delivery** — `auth-service`, unknown, confidence 0.45, plausible
   - Supporting: [ev_4, ev_7, ev_18] · Contradicting: [ev_17, ev_19]
   - auth-service error rate increased simultaneously, but logs showed no internal server errors (5xx), pointing toward client-side or verification failures resulting from missing codes.

## Facts
- auth-service otp_success_rate dropped from ~97.5% to ~68% starting around 2026-10-16T05:10:00.000Z. [ev_7]
- auth-service error rate increased from ~0.5% to ~4.5% starting at 2026-10-16T05:10:00.000Z. [ev_4, ev_18]
- notification-service logs show SMS messages accepted by sms-provider with status 202 during the incident window. [ev_3, ev_8, ev_12, ev_20]
- No deployments or configuration updates occurred on auth-service or notification-service prior to the incident. [ev_2]
- Historical incidents (PIR-2004, PIR-1602) indicate external SMS provider routing or delivery failures cause identical drops in OTP success rates. [ev_6]

## Inferences
- API acceptance (HTTP 202) by the SMS provider without successful downstream carrier delivery explains the drop in OTP success rates without a spike in notification-service error metrics. [ev_7, ev_8, ev_12]

## Assumptions
- The external SMS provider experienced downstream carrier delivery failures or severe DLR latency during the incident window.

## Timeline
- **2026-10-16T04:54:00.000Z (10:24 IST)** Log shipper agent upgraded on auth-service node pool (CHG-48221). [ev_2]
- **2026-10-16T05:10:00.000Z (10:40 IST)** OTP success rate drops and auth-service error rate begins to spike. [ev_4, ev_7]
- **2026-10-16T07:00:00.000Z (12:30 IST)** End of investigation window.

## Confidence
0.75: Supported by metrics, logs showing successful API acceptance by the SMS provider, and strong historical precedent (PIR-2004, PIR-1602). Direct carrier delivery logs are missing, relying on indirect inference.

## Gaps
- Direct carrier delivery receipt (DLR) logs and latency metrics from the external SMS provider. (impact: Prevents absolute confirmation of whether failure occurred at the carrier network level or provider gateway.)

## Recommended actions (not executed)
- **[now]** Contact the external SMS provider support to check for routing degradation, carrier filtering, or DLR delays. [ev_8, ev_12]
  - Why: API requests returned 202 Accepted, indicating the issue lies downstream of the provider API.
  - Verify: SMS provider confirms normal DLR rates and carrier delivery times.
- **[now]** Implement failover to secondary SMS provider if primary provider delivery rates remain degraded. [ev_6, ev_7]
  - Why: Historical incidents (PIR-2004) successfully resolved via secondary provider failover.
  - Verify: auth-service otp_success_rate recovers to >95%.
- **[next]** Add delivery-receipt latency and DLR failure rate alerts for notification-service. [ev_6]
  - Why: Early detection of downstream SMS delivery issues before user-facing OTP failures impact logins.
  - Verify: Alerts fire correctly during simulated downstream SMS delays.

Cited evidence: ev_2, ev_3, ev_4, ev_6, ev_7, ev_8, ev_12, ev_15, ev_16, ev_17, ev_18, ev_19, ev_20
Investigation window: 2026-10-16 10:00 IST to 2026-10-16 12:30 IST
